messages.subject: use of scale_x_ggtree() within facet_plot()
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to create a plot with 3 panels: a BEAST tree, a heatmap, and a dot plot. I applied scale_x_ggtree() to solve the issue with the time axis extending to the heatmap. However, there is a residual undesirable effect that it makes the scale for the other panel (a dot plot, in my case) disappear. This behavior can be seen using the example data from the vignettes as shown with the below code: 

# load package
library("ggtree")

#import data
beast_file <- system.file("examples/MCC_FluA_H3.tree", package="ggtree")
beast_tree <- read.beast(beast_file)

genotype_file <- system.file("examples/Genotype.txt", package="ggtree")
genotype <- read.table(genotype_file, sep="\t", stringsAsFactor=F)

# plot tree and heatmap
p <- ggtree(beast_tree, mrsd="2013-01-01") + geom_tiplab(size=2, align=TRUE, linesize=.5) + theme_tree2()
pp <- (p + scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0, 0.3))) %>%
    gheatmap(genotype, offset=8, width=0.6, colnames=FALSE) %>%
        scale_x_ggtree()

# add dot plot data
d1 <- data_frame(id = as_tibble(beast_tree)$label[!is.na(as_tibble(beast_tree)$label)], val = runif(76, min = 0, max = 10))

p3 <- facet_plot(pp,  panel="dot", data=d1, geom=geom_point, aes(x=val), color='firebrick')


You'll notice in p3, the axes for the tree and heatmap look great, but there is no dotplot axis. 

Does anyone have suggestions for how to shorten the x-axis on the dated tree so that it doesn't extend into the heatmap, while keeping a different x-axis on an additional panel?

Best,
Arianna
